A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OSDHuman/PERSONA study. All 11 pages of each are readable, including equations, nine figures and four tables. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original PERSONA dataset analyses, restoration experiments on PERSONA-Val and PERSONA-Test, and training-dataset and prompt-extractor ablations in Tables 1–4.

after.justification: v2 retains these original dataset analyses, restoration experiments and ablations, including quantitative results and visual restoration examples.

M1.justification: The HQ-ACF pipeline, OSDHuman architecture, HFIE conditioning, LoRA training and VSD objective remain unchanged. Sections 3.1–3.2 introduce no revised algorithm or model component.

E1.justification: Dataset sources, PERSONA training and evaluation coverage, and the LSDIR training comparison are retained. Figure 8 replaces an example within PERSONA-Test without establishing a distinct task or test scenario.

E2.justification: The comparison methods remain DiffBIR, SeeSR, PASD, ResShift, SinSR and OSEDiff, with the same retrained variants. Comparator membership in the visual comparisons and both ablations is also unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 4.2 revises the reported PERSONA training-set size from 109,052 to 109,053, consistently with other dataset descriptions. The 4,216-image validation set, 3,000-image test set, degradation pipeline, metrics and training budget remain unchanged. This count revision does not establish that training was rerun.

E4.justification: Figure 8 revises the challenging-case comparison of restoration fidelity by replacing its first portrait example. The training-dataset and prompt-extractor ablations in Tables 3–4 remain unchanged; no additional robustness or sensitivity analysis appears.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The reporting of aggregate metrics and the dataset-score standardization procedure are unchanged.

E6.justification: Figure 8 replaces its first input and corresponding restoration outputs, changing the reported qualitative results. All numerical entries in Tables 1–4 remain identical, including OSDHuman's PERSONA-Val PSNR of 22.41. The replacement does not demonstrate a performance change on the same input.

T1.justification: Equations 1–7 retain the same normalization, denoising, conditioning and loss definitions. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, proofs or formal results are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the claims about PERSONA's quality and diversity, HFIE-guided one-step restoration, and superior restoration performance. Replacing 'strong SOTA' with 'state-of-the-art' does not change the scientific claim.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning dataset suitability, prompt guidance, fidelity and competing methods remain unchanged. The new generic Impact Statement identifies no specific limitation, failure condition or applicability boundary.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces the incomplete prospective code/data statement with an explicit statement that both are available at the same repository address. This changes reported availability; actual access is not verified by the PDFs. Implementation settings and hardware disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Hu et al. (2022) for LoRA and Atmosukarto et al. (2024), Liu et al. (2025) and Sun et al. (2024) to the downstream-task motivation. These are limited citation additions without substantial repositioning of the contribution.

P1.justification: Section 2 receives localized terminology and wording edits, including explicitly naming PRCN and DiffBody. v2 also repairs smaller language issues and adds an Impact Statement, acknowledgments and conference information. The main narrative and section order remain stable.

P2.justification: Figure 8 replaces the first green-shirt portrait comparison, which had face-detail insets, with a denim-shirt portrait comparison without those insets. Figure 2 corrects the SinSR label. Added publication text and back matter cause limited reflow; table structures and the remaining visual examples are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves documentation through clearer code/data availability wording, explicit naming of prior methods and the previously missing LoRA attribution. The method and quantitative evidence remain unchanged, while Figure 8's replacement example provides no demonstrated strengthening of validation. The supported benefit is therefore limited to clarity and attribution.
